page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor providing 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via 2 threads per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache. Advanced instruction set support covers AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, along with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography.

The hardware configuration features an extreme compute-to-memory ratio of 1:1, offering 32.0 GB of system memory, which allocates exactly 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring reliance on remote network-attached block storage. There are no GPUs present. Network connectivity delivers a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear split between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-threaded execution is weak, with Geekbench single-core at 1001.0, stress-ng single-core at 1106.89, and single-threaded gzip compression at 19.05 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested servers. However, multi-core metrics scale up to average levels, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8847.0, a PassMark CPU score of 23037.68, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 23616.79. Memory bandwidth reaches 95.0 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 45.75 GB/sec for writes.

Given the low RAM-to-CPU ratio, the system offers cost efficiency specifically for compute tasks that scale horizontally across many threads without demanding substantial working memory per thread. The lack of bundled local disks and restricted per-core memory capacity makes it unsuited for large in-memory databases or caching layers. It is best suited for parallel batch processing, multi-threaded code compilation, static web server fleets, and lightweight multi-threaded data ingestion.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.8xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 server driven by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs. It features 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an aggressive 1:1 compute-to-memory profile of 1.0 GB per vCPU. The instance provides a 10 Gbps baseline network interface, includes no bundled local storage, and contains no hardware accelerators. Benchmark testing shows modest single-threaded performance countered by competitive multi-threaded capacity, scoring 23037.68 on PassMark CPU, 8847.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and achieving 22.46 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads. With hardware instruction extensions including AVX-512 and AES, the instance is structured to deliver resource-efficient multi-threaded compute without the overhead of unused memory. It is appropriate for CPU-bound tasks such as multi-threaded compiling, parallel batch processing, and static web serving.
